$comment: VM tier menu — SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the shorthand VM sizes (operator spec, 2026-07-31). Consumed by resolve_vm_tier() in scripts/lib/provision-helpers.sh (bash/jq, drives --tier in oci-create-vm.sh + provision.sh) and by the #2467 Admin → VMs panel tier selector, which should display est_monthly_usd next to each tier at provisioning time. est_monthly_usd is a BALLPARK: raw PAYG marginal cost per month at the pricing_basis rates. The OCI always-free allowance (4 OCPU + 24 GB A1 compute, 200 GB total block storage) absorbs roughly one VM's worth (~$60/mo of value), so the FIRST VM in the tenancy runs ~free; every additional VM costs about its est_monthly_usd.
$comment_sessions: Per-tier open-session counts and the machine block (issue #4417) come from a load test on 2026-10-06: one scratch VM per tier (lite, standard, pro; Ubuntu 24.04 arm64, the shipped daemon unit), each session a worktree spawn plus one real model turn. max_sessions = the open sessions the tier held before a spawn failed or the 50-session ceiling stopped it. recommended_sessions = the open sessions that stayed healthy when a third of them ran builds (typecheck, web tests, single-binary build) and a third ran repo tool work. Ultra was not measured: its counts are derived from the measured coefficients. machine_minimum / machine_recommended are the standard and pro shapes with their measured counts; disk is the measured base install plus about 0.75 GiB per open session of the test repository, at the tier maximum, rounded up to 10 GB. The disk figures count open sessions only. An archived session keeps its worktree on disk (0.75 GiB each in this test, the same as an open one), and only deleting the session frees it, after a 10-day recovery window. Retention has no upper bound, so no fixed figure covers it (PM ruling R-DISK, #4754). In the test, standard reached 40.5 GiB with 8 sessions open because its idle leg had left 33 archived worktrees on disk. Counts are per Hapimatic instance. docs/guide/installation.md § Machine requirements repeats machine_minimum / machine_recommended, the lite, standard and pro counts and the 0.75 GiB per working copy: update it when they change.

pricing_basis.formula: ocpus * a1_ocpu_usd_per_month + memory_gb * a1_mem_gb_usd_per_month + boot_volume_gb * block_storage_gb_usd_per_month

$comment_pilot: The pilot tier and tenant_default_tier (issue #3993, ruling 2026-09-29, price arithmetic in #4350): the tenant target's standard configuration, 4 OCPU / 16 GB / 256 GB boot. The tenant golden image (#3994) is captured from this shape. default_tier stays the operator choice (pro). pilot sits AFTER pro on purpose: vm_tier_from_shape() (provision-helpers.sh) ignores the boot volume, so a 4/16 shape ties pro and pilot and the stable sort keeps the FIRST, pro; pilot first would read every Pro VM as pilot and drop it from DESKTOP_TIER_ALLOWLIST. scripts/test-vm-tiers.sh (t) pins the order. The web menu (web/src/lib/vmTiers.ts VM_TIER_IDS) lists ultra/pro/standard/lite only, so pilot is not offered there.

swap.$comment: Swap on every cloud VM (issue #4784): one compressed-RAM zram device, zstd, sized at half of the VM's MemTotal at each boot, with vm.swappiness 180 and vm.page-cluster 0. No disk swapfile: session memory holds OAuth tokens and handoff secrets, and zram never writes them to the boot volume or into a golden image; the small tiers are also already I/O-bound. Per tier that is about Ultra 12 / Pro 8 / Standard 4 / Lite 2 GB of zram (half of memory_gb; Pro measured 7.8 GiB from a MemTotal of 15,951 MiB). Boot-volume cost is 0 GB, so the disk figures are unchanged and still count open sessions only (PM ruling R-DISK, #4754); the only disk cost is linux-modules-extra (about 0.13 GiB per installed kernel) on 6.x Oracle kernels whose zram module lives there. Written by infrastructure/cloud-vm/hapi-swap-v1.sh (cloud-init, provision.sh Phase 5.1), checked by reconcile-vm.sh --surface swap and the VM parity check; scripts/test-swap-v1.sh keeps these fields equal to the script's print-config. Full table: docs/internal/architecture/cloud-provisioning.md § Swap.
